sector_model: Payments software with leverage and lumpy license revenue: P/E, FCF after capitalized software, net debt, backlog, license timing, CEO change.
thesis: ACI Worldwide (Nasdaq: ACIW), payments and bill-payment software. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read. Q3 revenue 426.8M (-11.5%) as license revenue fell 41% (94.8M vs 162.0M); SaaS and platform revenue +4.6%; operating income 52.4M vs 127.7M; net income 32.5M vs 91.3M. 60-month backlog 7,374M vs 7,259M at 2025-12-31 (committed 2,123M vs 2,304M). 8-K 5.02 (filed 2026-11-18): CEO Warsop resigned effective 11-18 (leaves 12-18), CFO Leibrock is interim CEO and stopped being chief accounting officer, board chair became executive chairman. Stock fell from 58.93 (11-17) to 50.41 (11-20), -14.5%. Close 50.41 x 100,194,536 shares (2026-11-02) = 5.05B = 30.2x TTM NI 167.0M; TTM FCF 331.8M after capitalized software (6.6%). Debt 817.0M vs cash 218.8M. Business is cash generative; the question is whether Q3 license drop is timing or demand, and why the CEO left.
counterthesis: Reported TTM earnings already reflect weak Q3; license revenue is lumpy and the CFO is now also interim CEO, which concentrates roles during a transition and a CAO change. Reason for CEO resignation is stated only as no disagreement. OCF benefited from 47.7M receivable collections (accrued receivables from earlier licenses). Committed backlog is shrinking. Debt of 817M with 722.5M due 2029; SBC 54M over 9M is large against NI.
invalidation: Downgrade if next quarter's license revenue stays near Q3 level, committed backlog keeps falling, or the CEO exit is linked to accounting or guidance problems; upgrade case needs verified peers, normalized license revenue, and verified quotes.
